    Finite source-by-source normalization of contour functions #

    Isolate the global induction in Roiter's vanishing argument. On a finite quiver, if every contour function can be normalized at one more source while preserving a finite set of already normalized sources, then every contour function is exact. The remaining representation-theoretic content is the local source-normalization step.

    source
    def LargeIndecomposable.ContourFunctionNormalizedAtSource {k : Type u} [Field k] {Q : Type v} [Quiver Q] (R : PathContourRelation Q) (c : ↥(contourScalarFunctionSubgroup R)) (x : Q) :
    Prop

    A contour function is normalized at x when it has value one on every related pair of paths starting at x.
